item.title: Severe Tropical Cyclone Hayley forecast to make landfall over the Dampier Peninsula, Australia
item.description: Severe Tropical Cyclone Hayley is forecast to make landfall over the northern Dampier Peninsula, Western Australia, late on Tuesday, December 30, 2025, as a Category 3 system. The cyclone is expected to bring destructive winds, heavy rainfall, and flash flooding across parts of the west Kimberley coast. Source

item.title: Earth-directed CME from M4.2 flare forecast to produce G1 geomagnetic storm on New Year’s Day
item.description: A coronal mass ejection (CME) associated with an M4.2 solar flare from Region 4317 is expected to produce a G1 - Minor geomagnetic storm as it grazes Earth late on December 31 into early January 1, 2026. Source

item.title: Three killed by floods and landslides in Andalusia, Spain
item.description: At least three people have been killed by severe floods and landslides in Spain between December 28--29, 2025. Source

item.title: Subtropical moisture and re-intensified atmospheric river to impact California through New Year’s weekend
item.description: A surge of subtropical moisture is forecast to bring moderate to heavy rain to southern and central California on Wednesday, December 31, 2025, with rain spreading north on Thursday, January 1, 2026. A stronger system with a re-intensified atmospheric river is expected to make landfall early Friday, January 2, bringing heavier precipitation along the northern and central California coast. Source

item.title: Evacuation warnings issued for Los Angeles County burn scar areas ahead of New Year storm
item.description: Evacuation warnings were issued for Los Angeles County, California for multiple burn scars across the region as an atmospheric river brings in the threat of flash floods and debris flows through New Year's Day. Source

item.title: Back to back atmospheric rivers forecast to bring heavy rain and mountain snow to California
item.description: Heavy rain and snow are forecast across California and Sierra Nevada through January 4, 2026. The first wave will target southern California with subtropical moisture, followed by a stronger system forecast to bring heavy rain and snowfall across central and northern regions of the state. Source

item.title: Long-duration M7.1 solar flare erupts from AR 4324
item.description: A long-duration solar flare measuring M7.1 at its peak erupted from Active Region 4324 at 13:51 UTC on December 31, 2025. The event started at 13:12 and ended at 14:11 UTC. Source

item.title: Strong M6.0 earthquake hits near the east coast of Honshu, Japan
item.description: A strong and shallow earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.0 hit near the east coast of Honshu, Japan at 14:26 UTC on December 31, 2025. The agency is reporting a depth of 19.3 km (12 miles). EMSC is reporting M6.0 at a depth of 19 km (11.8 miles). Source

item.title: Alberta clipper reinforces lake-effect snow as heavy rain targets southern California into the New Year
item.description: A surge of Arctic air, reinforced lake-effect snowfall, and an atmospheric river are forecast to affect large portions of the United States from December 31, 2025, into January 2, 2026. Heavy snow is expected downwind of the Great Lakes and across parts of the Northeast, while southern California faces a flash flood risk as an atmospheric river moves onshore around New Year’s Day. Source

item.title: Shallow M6.0 earthquake hits southeast Indian Ridge
item.description: A shallow earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.0 struck the southeast Indian Ridge at 01:53 UTC on January 1, 2026. The agency is reporting a depth of 10 km (6.2 miles). EMSC is reporting the same magnitude and depth. Source
